instruction: UV Master Work-On-Clone Workflow The opened `scene.obj` contains a ZBrush Tool whose first (and only) SubTool, named Subject, is a head-shaped polymesh at approximately 32000 quad faces (with triangle caps at the poles). The mesh has no UVs, no polygroups beyond default, and no polypaint. Using the opened OBJ in ZBrush, use UV Master's Work-On-Clone workflow to unwrap a decimated copy and copy the UVs back onto the high-res original, then export two OBJs: the high-res original with its new UVs as `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\high_uv.obj`, and the decimated clone with the same UVs as `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\low_uv.obj`. Write both files to `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop` with the filenames listed above. The two exported OBJs must satisfy: - Each contains exactly one SubTool named Subject. - `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\high_uv.obj` vertex and face counts equal the input's; every vertex position matches the input within 1e-5 BU. - `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\low_uv.obj` face count is in [18000, 22000]. - Both OBJs contain `vt` records and every face references `vt` indices. - All UV coordinates of both files lie in [0,1] x [0,1] (with tiny float slack). - The bidirectional Chamfer distance between the two OBJs' UV point clouds is at most 0.01.
